extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and educated readers interested in American political institutions, constitutional law, and comparative politics
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive late-19th/early-20th century treatise describing the structure, practice, and forces of American national and state government, with appended constitutional extracts (Oklahoma, California). Intended as a systematic overview for European and American readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three essential aspects of a national commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three main things to know about a national commonwealth: (1) its framework and constitutional machinery, (2) the methods by which it is worked, and (3) the forces which move it and direct its course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three dimensions as the organising principles when analysing a national government: start with structure, then practice, then underlying social/political forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational plan for describing American government
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with the National government (President, Congress, Courts), then describe relations to the States; next treat State governments, then the party system (as a second body of political machinery), public opinion (the people's mind and conscience), illustrative historical instances, and finally non-political institutions relevant to national character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the author's prescribed chapter/part sequence for a comprehensive treatment: Part I National, Part II State, Part III Parties, Part IV Public Opinion, Part V Examples and Questions, Part VI Non-political institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological approach to political description
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the deductive method and ready-made theories; favour presentation of facts, letting them 'speak for themselves'; be cautious in inference and avoid bold generalizations unsupported by observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should aim to present concrete facts, trace phenomena to their sources when needed, and allow philosophically minded readers to build theories from the material rather than imposing speculative conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness without exhaustiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek to be comprehensive in scope but not exhaustive in minute detail; omit topics already well-covered elsewhere or those beyond the author's special competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise what is necessary to make political life and national character intelligible to the intended audience; cover less familiar or more illuminating topics in greater depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal incorporation by general law
rubrics_metrics.description: Municipal corporations shall not be created by special laws; the Legislature, by general laws, shall provide for the incorporation and organization of cities and towns and the classification of same in proportion to population, subject to the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits ad hoc special-legislation for municipal creation; requires general enabling statutes to regulate municipal incorporation and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for a city to obtain special charter (board of freeholders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any city with more than two thousand inhabitants may frame a charter for its own government by electing a board of freeholders (two from each ward) who must prepare and propose a charter within ninety days; the proposed charter must be published and submitted to the city's qualified electors and, if ratified, submitted to the Governor for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charter proposal steps: election of board of freeholders → drafting within 90 days → publication (21 days if daily; 3 consecutive issues if weekly) → submission to electors (30–20 days after first publication window) → majority ratification → Governor approval → deposit of certified copies (Secretary of State and city archives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of freeholders election by petition and preliminary vote
rubrics_metrics.description: A legislative authority may call an election of freeholders or must call it within ten days after a petition demanding it is filed, signed by qualified electors equal to 25% of votes cast at the preceding general municipal election; at the election a preliminary vote is taken on proceeding with drafting the charter, and unless a majority vote to proceed, further proceedings are void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a 25% petition threshold to trigger freeholders' election and a majority preliminary approval by electors to continue the charter adoption process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative and referendum reserved to municipalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers of the initiative and referendum, reserved by the Constitution to the people of the State and respective counties and districts, are hereby reserved to the people of every municipal corporation with reference to all legislative authority it may exercise and charter amendments for its own government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Municipalities and their residents retain direct-democracy powers for municipal legislation and charter changes, parallel to state-level initiative/referendum rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature threshold for municipal initiative/referendum petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Every petition for either the initiative or referendum in municipal government must be signed by qualified electors residing in the municipality equal to 25% of the total number of votes cast at the next preceding election and filed with the chief executive officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a uniform 25% petitioner threshold for municipal direct-democracy measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative enactment procedure for municipal ordinances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition demands enactment of an ordinance (other than franchise matters), the chief executive presents it to the legislative body; unless granted more than 30 days before the next election at which city officers are elected, the ordinance shall be submitted to the qualified electors at that election and, if a majority vote for it, it becomes law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timeline and the default path to popular vote if the legislative body does not adopt the petitioned ordinance in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referendum procedure on municipal ordinances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition demands a referendum on any ordinance (other than franchise matters), the chief executive shall submit the ordinance to the qualified electors at the next general municipal election; if a majority of electors voting do not vote for the ordinance, it is repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives citizens the power to demand popular review and potential repeal of legislative acts via petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of municipal charter by petition and vote
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition demands an amendment to a charter, the chief executive shall submit the amendment to the qualified electors at the next election of any officer of the corporation; if a majority voting approve, the amendment becomes part of the charter upon Governor approval and proper filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charter amendments via petition follow a similar petition→popular vote→Governor approval→filing sequence as original charters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchise grants require direct popular approval and have term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No municipal corporation shall grant, extend, or renew a franchise without approval of a majority of qualified electors resident within its corporate limits voting at a general or special election; no franchise may be granted, extended, or renewed for a longer term than twenty-five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires voter approval for municipal franchises and caps franchise terms at 25 years; legislative bodies may submit franchise questions or special elections called on 30 days' notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition threshold to demand a franchise election
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition signed by qualified electors equal to 25% of the votes cast at the next preceding general municipal election demanding that a franchise be granted, extended, or renewed requires the chief executive to call a special election within ten days to submit the question to voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again establishes a 25% petition trigger for putting franchise questions to popular vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal corporations' power to engage in business
rubrics_metrics.description: Every municipal corporation shall have the right to engage in any business or enterprise which may be engaged in by a person, firm, or corporation by virtue of a franchise from said corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms municipal authority to conduct business activities analogous to private franchise-granting operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reservation of control over public highways and prohibition of exclusive franchises
rubrics_metrics.description: No grant, extension, or renewal of any franchise or other use of streets, alleys, or other public grounds or ways shall divest the State or its subdivisions of control and regulation of such use; power to regulate charges for public services shall not be surrendered; no exclusive franchise shall ever be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuing public/regulatory control over municipal public-ways and forbids exclusive monopolies; municipal grants cannot relieve state's regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eight-hour day for public employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight hours shall constitute a day's work in all cases of employment by and on behalf of the State or any county or municipality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mandate setting a maximum standard workday length for public-sector employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contracting for convict labor
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting of convict labor is hereby prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bars public contracting systems that use convict labor as contracted services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child labor prohibition under age fifteen in hazardous occupations
rubrics_metrics.description: The employment of children under the age of fifteen years in any occupation injurious to health or morals or especially hazardous to life or limb is hereby prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a baseline age and hazard-based restriction on child employment, delegating specifics to implementing legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of underground work for boys under sixteen and for women; eight-hour underground day
rubrics_metrics.description: Boys under the age of sixteen years, and women and girls, shall not be employed underground in mines; except in emergencies, eight hours shall constitute a day's work underground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific protections for vulnerable workers in mining, with an eight-hour limit except emergency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative duty to protect employees' health and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislature shall pass laws to protect the health and safety of employees in factories, in mines, and on railroads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional command for occupational health & safety statutory schemes for major industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributory negligence and assumption of risk as jury questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The defense of contributory negligence or of assumption of risk shall, in all cases whatsoever, be a question of fact and shall be left to the jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates determinations of negligence/assumption-of-risk defenses to factfinders (juries) rather than as legal questions for judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of action for death is never abrogated
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of action to recover damages for injuries resulting in death shall never be abrogated, and the amount recoverable shall not be subject to any statutory limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects wrongful-death claims from legislative abolition and forbids statutory caps on recoverable damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of constitutional benefits in contract void
rubrics_metrics.description: Any provision of a contract, express or implied, by which any of the benefits of this Constitution is sought to be waived shall be null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents contractual forfeiture of constitutional protections; constitutional rights cannot be contractually waived away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clauses making statutory notice/demand conditions precedent void
rubrics_metrics.description: Any contract provision stipulating for notice or demand other than such as may be provided by law, as a condition precedent to establishing any claim, demand, or liability, shall be null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guards against private contract terms that would displace statutory procedural protections or limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling a constitutional convention requires prior referendum approval; convention proposals require voter ratification
rubrics_metrics.description: No convention shall be called by the Legislature to propose alterations, revisions, or amendments to this Constitution unless the law providing for such convention is first approved by the people on a referendum vote; any amendments proposed by such convention shall be submitted to electors and approved by a majority before taking effect. The question of calling a convention must be submitted at least once every twenty years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures popular consent at both the call-to-convention stage and the ratification-of-proposals stage; periodic check (at least every 20 years) for convention calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend the Constitution by initiative petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The article shall not impair the right of the people to amend the Constitution by a vote upon an initiative petition therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves direct-democracy route for constitutional amendment via initiative petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and contractual maximum rates of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal rate of interest shall not exceed six per cent per annum in the absence of any contract as to rate; by contract parties may agree upon any rate not to exceed ten per cent per annum, and until reduced by the Legislature those rates (6% legal, 10% maximum contract) are the legal and maximum contract rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets constitutional ceiling/defaults for interest rates absent legislative action; allows contracts up to specified maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homestead sale and mortgage protections (spousal consent and foreclosure exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner, if married, shall not sell the homestead without the consent of his or her spouse given as prescribed by law; nothing shall prohibit mortgaging the homestead with the spouse joining; foreclosure sale to satisfy such mortgage is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affords married-spouse protections against unilateral sale of homestead while permitting mortgage encumbrance and foreclosure to enforce mortgage claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: California Constitution Article XIX (regulation and exclusion of Chinese and certain aliens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions directing the Legislature to prescribe regulations to protect the State from burdens and evils arising from certain aliens (vagrants, paupers, criminals, contagious disease sufferers), to impose conditions for their residence and removal; prohibition on corporations employing Chinese or Mongolians; prohibition on Chinese employment on public works except as criminal punishment; declaration that presence of foreigners ineligible for U.S. citizenship is dangerous and the Legislature shall discourage their immigration; Asiatic 'coolieism' forever prohibited and contracts for coolie labour void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clauses exemplify explicit xenophobic constitutional restrictions (late-19th-century context) on immigration, employment of specified races/aliens, and delegation of removal/enforcement powers to state and municipal authorities.
